clue.text: No-good bums, at first, keep feeding invalid dope

indicators.note: something no good is faulty, so the word it describes is broken up and rearranged
at first points to the opening letter of the word that follows it
feeding one thing into another puts it inside, so these letters go into the middle of the outer word

blocks.note: the word as written, to be rearranged
the opening letter of keep
null and void: no longer valid

explanation.surface: Useless layabouts keep passing drugs to a sick person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like a drug, as the puzzle's theme wants, but here it means a fool. 'Invalid' looks like a sick person, but means void.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, and numbskull is another informal word for an idiot.

clue.text: Savings account gets returns when invested in nitrogen, for example

indicators.note: returns means comes back, so the word before it is read backwards
money invested in something is put into it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: taken as written, to be read backwards
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen
e.g. is the usual abbreviation for for example

explanation.surface: A savings account earns interest when the money is put into a gas.
explanation.walkthrough: STEG goes inside NEG, between its E and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is money put aside as a reserve for the future.

clue.text: Alien in Massachusetts train wreck

indicators.note: a wreck leaves things smashed and scattered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: MA is the postal abbreviation for Massachusetts
taken as written

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial is caught up in a rail crash in Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: A Martian is a being from Mars, the stock example of an extraterrestrial.

clue.text: Take precedence in speaker's choice between bouillon and grain?

indicators.note: a speaker's version is what is heard, so the words are matched by sound

blocks.note: bouillon is a clear soup and a grain is a seed, so the choice is soup or seed

explanation.surface: A diner must decide whether broth or cereal comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To supersede is to replace and so rank ahead of what went before.

clue.text: Disturbed one from Quebec and un Américain capturing the heart of Canadians

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so the middle letter goes between the two words
the heart is the centre, so only the middle letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: un is French for one, and Quebec is French-speaking
what an American calls un, translated back into English
the fifth of the nine letters

explanation.surface: A troubled Québécois and an American hold a Canadian at the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The French and English words for one sit either side of D.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone undone is upset and thrown into distress, as in emotionally unravelled.

clue.text: Scurrilous smear lay outside Buddhist cloister

indicators.note: scurrilous means coarse and disorderly, so the next word is knocked out of shape
outside says the word before it goes round the jumbled letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A slanderous rumour was spread about a Buddhist monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scurrilous smear' reads as one phrase, but the adjective is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamasery is a monastery of lamas, the monks of Tibetan Buddhism.

clue.text: Ark housing small crow

indicators.note: a building housing someone holds them inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: Noah's ark was a boat
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Noah's ark has a little crow aboard among the animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' looks like the bird on the ark, but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to brag loudly about a success, which is what boasting means.

clue.text: Senator's dog

blocks.note: first meaning: Barbara, US senator for California from 1993 to 2017
second meaning: a muscular, short-haired German breed

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a politician's pet, but the senator and the dog share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of a well-known Californian senator is also a German dog breed.

clue.text: A vehicle I have is potentially dangerous

blocks.note: taken as written
a bus is a road vehicle
the contraction I've, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A car I own could be a hazard on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive behaviour, violent or harmful, is a threat to those around it.

clue.text: According to his fans, Bruce Willis finally goes after malfunctioning she-bot

indicators.note: a malfunctioning machine is out of order, so the word is shuffled into a new one
finally points to the last letter of the word before it
goes after fixes the order, putting that letter at the end

blocks.note: taken as written, hyphen dropped, to be rearranged
the final letter of Willis

explanation.surface: Fans say actor Bruce Willis ends up fighting a broken female robot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition borrows Bruce from Bruce Willis: it is Bruce Springsteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruce Springsteen's admirers have long called the rock singer by this nickname.

clue.text: Grazed car, broken into, went too fast

indicators.note: a broken thing is in pieces, so the word before it is rearranged
into tells us the rearranged word is placed inside the following phrase's word

blocks.note: sped is the past tense of speed, to drive over the limit
the word as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A car that was broken into got grazed by someone speeding past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken into' reads as a burglary, but 'broken' is the rearranging signal and 'into' the inserting one.
explanation.definitionFit: To graze a knee or a car is to scrape its surface lightly in passing.

clue.text: Ruined tux, covered with mud and hash

indicators.note: a ruined garment is wrecked, so the word after it is jumbled into a new order
being covered with something means it surrounds you, so the outer word wraps around

blocks.note: mire is deep mud or a bog
the word as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dinner jacket is ruined, smeared with mud and cannabis resin.
explanation.walkthrough: Tux is short for tuxedo, a dinner jacket. 'Hash' plays on the drug theme but means a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A hash is a jumbled medley of things, as in making a hash of something, so a mixture.

clue.text: They have moved away from streaming illegally

indicators.note: doing something illegally means not by the rules, so the word is put into an unlawful new order

blocks.note: the word as written, nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: People have stopped watching pirated shows online.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as quitting illegal downloading; the definition is people who have left their country.
explanation.definitionFit: Emigrants are people who have left their homeland to settle in another country.

clue.text: Letter from Athens describing fashionable beast

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw around it, so the outer word goes round the inner one

blocks.note: rho is the Greek letter equivalent to R
what is in is in fashion

explanation.surface: A Greek letter writes about a trendy animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing around.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhinoceros is a large, heavy wild animal, the kind of creature called a beast.

clue.text: Grass destroyed urge to protect nest's boundaries

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so the word after it is rebuilt in a new order
protecting something means surrounding it, so the jumbled letters wrap round the others
the boundaries of a word are its two edges, so only its first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the first and last letters of nest, its two edges

explanation.surface: The lawn was ruined by an animal's instinct to guard its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like lawn, or the drug the theme suggests, but it is the surname of the German novelist, and the answer is his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Günter Grass, the German writer of The Tin Drum, won the 1999 Nobel Prize; his forename is clued by his surname.

clue.text: Doobies, perhaps stock at the center of cybershop

indicators.note: the center of a word is its middle, so only its central letters are kept

blocks.note: stock is a cooking broth made from bones or vegetables
the three central letters of the nine-letter cybershop

explanation.surface: A website sells marijuana joints and keeps a stock of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Doobies are joints in slang, but the Doobie Brothers are an American rock band, so a Doobie is one of the band's members.
explanation.definitionFit: The members of the rock band The Doobie Brothers are examples of the plural noun, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Weighty book about punk: "Here's Nirvana, for instance"

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer word wraps round the rest
punk means worthless or rebellious, roughing up the word that follows into a new order

blocks.note: a tome is a big heavy volume
taken as written, apostrophe dropped, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hefty book on punk rock offers Nirvana as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: Nirvana looks like punk's example, and 'Here's' like a pointer, but both are wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana, the Seattle grunge band of Kurt Cobain, was a trio: a group of three.

clue.text: Father's weapon provides a means of access

blocks.note: pa is father, with the possessive s
a sword is a bladed weapon

explanation.surface: Dad's sword lets someone get in.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret word you must give before you are allowed entry, to a building or a computer.

clue.text: Oral proverb: "Reach across for pot"

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so the pieces are judged by how they are said rather than spelt

blocks.note: a saw is an old saying or proverb, and to span is to reach across; run together they are said like a kitchen utensil

explanation.surface: A spoken saying urges someone to stretch over and grab some marijuana.
explanation.walkthrough: SAW followed by SPAN, said quickly, sounds like SAUCEPAN. 'Pot' plays on the drug theme but is the cooking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot is a deep cooking vessel, and a saucepan is one with a long handle.

clue.text: Nobel-winning chemist who taught at UC Berkeley snarled, "Go Bears!"

definitions.text: Nobel-winning chemist who taught at UC Berkeley

indicators.note: snarled means tangled as well as growled, so the quoted words are knotted into a new order

blocks.note: the Berkeley sports cheer, taken as written

explanation.surface: A Berkeley professor growls the college team's cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: The California Golden Bears are Berkeley's sports teams; 'snarled' looks like a growl but means tangled.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenn Seaborg shared the 1951 Nobel Prize for discovering plutonium and other elements, working at Berkeley.

clue.text: Dirty relative with a stain in the rear

indicators.note: the rear is the back end, so only the last letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: an uncle is a relative
taken as written
the final letter of stain

explanation.surface: A grubby family member has a mark on the seat of his trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclean is soiled and not washed, which is what dirty means.

clue.text: No sir — cop ultimately returned a joint

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word before it is kept
something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of cop

explanation.surface: A man refuses a police officer who hands back a marijuana cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: NOSIR plus P, read backwards, gives PRISON. Joint is American slang for a jail, not the drug the theme suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a joint is a place, and in particular the jail where convicts are locked up.

clue.text: One way to have fish is Amish stew

indicators.note: a stew mixes ingredients together, so the letters before it are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Amish cooks serve their fish in a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' looks like the dish in the definition's picture, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sashimi is Japanese raw fish sliced thin, a style of serving seafood.

clue.text: Geometrical shape devoid of dramatic conflict?

blocks.note: non- is the prefix meaning without
agon is the Greek word for the central contest in a classical play

explanation.surface: A shape so dull it has no drama in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags reading the shape's name as two parts, NON plus AGON.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a plane figure with nine straight sides and nine angles.

clue.text: Never mind swallowing rats or bugs

indicators.note: swallowing means taking inside, so the phrase before it holds the letters within it

blocks.note: the letters run from inside never into mind

explanation.surface: Don't worry about the pests being eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Never mind' reads as a shrug, but it is the phrase that holds the answer: neVER MINd.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermin are small animals and insects such as rodents and lice that are pests.

clue.text: Coat's tangled up with scarf

indicators.note: something tangled up is knotted into disorder, so its letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the word as written, apostrophe dropped, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A coat has become knotted together with a scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad neckscarf or cravat, looped under the chin.

clue.text: Where Scarlett O'Hara was clutching one crown

indicators.note: clutching means holding tight, so the outer word grips the inner one

blocks.note: Tara is the O'Hara plantation in Gone with the Wind
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Scarlett O'Hara clings to a crown at her home.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled headband, a small crown worn by royalty or brides.

clue.text: Scottish author, 77, running around Tay's source

indicators.note: a river's source is where it begins, so only the first letter is kept
around says one piece is wrapped about another, which sits inside it

blocks.note: 77 is two sevens
the opening letter of Tay, a Scottish river
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A 77-year-old Scottish writer is jogging along the River Tay.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay is Scotland's longest river; read 77 as two sevens rather than an age.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson, who wrote Treasure Island, was born in Edinburgh.

clue.text: Herb donuts captivate Shakespearean princess

indicators.note: to captivate is literally to take captive, so the outer letters hold the other word inside

blocks.note: two donuts are ring-shaped, like two letter Os
Regan is one of King Lear's daughters

explanation.surface: Pastries win over a princess from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' plays on the drug theme, but it is the cooking kind here.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic plant whose dried leaves are used in Italian cooking.

clue.text: The sound of a pet is due to follow me

indicators.note: to follow means to come after, setting the order of the two pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
money that is due is still owing

explanation.surface: Someone hears their pet and says it's their turn next.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's cry is a meow, so a cat making noise is heard meowing.

clue.text: Horse comes back in Germany? Yes: it is evoked in eight Across definitions

definitions.text: it is evoked in eight Across definitions

indicators.note: coming back means going the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a nag is an old horse
ja is the German for yes

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a horse returns in Germany, and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme answer: dope, hash, grass, Doobies, pot, joint, Herb and weed all hint at cannabis in the Across clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganja is a slang name for marijuana, the drug those eight Across definitions play on.

clue.text: Head of department and student at Yale using weed

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of department
taken as written
Yale students are called Elis, after Elihu Yale
someone using a drug is said to be on it

explanation.surface: A department chief and a Yale student are smoking marijuana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' plays on the drug theme, but it is a garden weed here.
explanation.definitionFit: The dandelion is a yellow-flowered plant that gardeners treat as a lawn pest.
